questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman diagnosed with limited systemic sclerosis 5 years ago is seen in the clinic. Which of the following examination findings would raise your suspicion of pulmonary arterial hypertension?
questions.stemHtml: A 38-year-old woman diagnosed with limited systemic sclerosis 5 years ago is seen in the clinic. Which of the following examination findings would raise your suspicion of pulmonary arterial hypertension?
questions.solution: Correct Option C: Loud S2 Pulmonary arterial hypertension occurs in about 12% of patients with limited systemic sclerosis due to obliterative vascular disease. Patients are most commonly asymptomatic but may present with dyspnoea, syncope and chest (anginal) pain. On examination, a small volume pulse, peripheral vasoconstriction with cool extremities reflect the low cardiac output. A right ventricular heave occurs where there is right ventricular hypertrophy and this creates an 'a' wave in the neck veins. The pulmonary component of the second heart sound becomes prominent as the pressure increases. A third heart sound heralds the onset of right heart failure when the central venous pressure rises with fluid retention and peripheral oedema. Dilatation of the right ventricle leads to tricuspid incompetence which produces a systolic murmur and a 'V' wave in the JVP. This accelerates the right heart failure with worsening peripheral oedema and pulsatile swelling of the liver. Incorrect Options: Option A- Bi-basal crackles: Bi-basal crackles is a feature of Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, as well as in lung fibrosis, pneumonia. Option B- Double apex beat: A loud first heart sound, slow rising pulse and sustained or double apex beat are all features of aortic stenosis. Option D- Slow rising pulse: A loud first heart sound, slow rising pulse and sustained or double apex beat are all features of aortic stenosis. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.solution: Correct Option D - Takayasu's arteritis: Presentation of Takayasu's arteritis is often with constitutional symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats and arthralgias. Symptoms related to ischaemia may include ischaemic stroke and/or transient ischaemic attacks, visual disturbances and rarely in children-claudication. The aortic arch is commonly involved, but the thoracoabdominal aorta and its branches, as well as the pulmonary artery, can be affected. If the aortic arch is involved there may be differential BP and absent or diminished upper arm pulses with bruits over the diseased vessels. Post-stenotic dilatations may result in bounding pulses. However, cervical rib usually presents with other signs, such as visible or palpable bony protrusions in the neck area, which are not mentioned in the case. Additionally, the laboratory findings and weight loss are not typical of cervical rib, making it a less likely diagnosis. questions.solution: Correct Option C - Refer for right heart catheterization: The British thoracic society guidelines recommend that echocardiogram and pulmonary function tests including DLCO should be performed annually.
